text:
ana-ml: heads up — running a slab allocator + KV-affinity experiment for 4-model co-residency on GPU0. seeing intermittent OOMs when batch=4.

mike-runtime: config? slab size / workspace / reserve?

ana-ml: slab_size=256MB, workspace_cap=1.5GB, reserve=128MB. kernel selector patch enabled that prefers fp16-vectorized kernels for llama2-13b variants.

kevin-profiling: can you paste the quick perf snapshot? p95/99 numbers and a short flame or nvprof output would help. did you enable prewarm-swap?

ana-ml: quick run output: ```
# ./run_inference --models=mA,mB,mC,mD --batch=4 --kv-affinity=slot --prewarm=false
latency_p50: 82ms
latency_p95: 420ms
latency_p99: 980ms
oom_events: 1 (swap->evict)
GPU0 mem at OOM: 11.9GiB / 12.0GiB
log: "Alloc failed: requested 240MB, no free slab >= 192MB"
```

raj-alloc: that log screams fragmentation. slab_size 256MB + big workspace + kv caches pinned = small scatter. try lowering slab_size to 192MB or enabling slab_defrag=true. also set reuse_threshold=0.25 so buffers <25% free get reused.

kevin-profiling: i also see kernel switch causing larger peak memory (vectorized/temp buffers). the kernel selection added a temp buffer of ~80MB for fused attention in some sequence lengths. check kernel profile for seq=512.

ana-ml: noted. re-ran with slab_size=192MB, reuse_threshold=0.25, prewarm-swap=true.

oom-bot: OOM detected on GPU0 at 1819876555 during model-swap (process=serving-worker-12). Auto-evicted KV cache chunk (128MB).

mike-runtime: interesting — eviction freed enough for the allocation but you lost cache hits. that explains p99 spikes. consider reserving a small eviction pool (reserve=256MB) to avoid mid-request evictions.

raj-alloc: another option: soft-isolate models by kv-affinity slots. keep hot-models in slot0 with exclusive slab slices, allow cold models to share a smaller pooled slab. reduces cross-model fragmentation.

kevin-profiling: here's a short diffsnippet that reproduces the temp buffer blowup for fused-attn:
```
# when seq=512, fused kernel allocs tmp_buf=80MB per stream
kernel: fused_attn_v2 -> tmp_alloc = ceil(ctx_len/64)*X
```
We should prefer the alternative kernel at seq=512 when gpu_free < 200MB. add that as a heuristic in kernel selector.

sophia-sre: FYI grafana — tail latency alert triggered for this experiment at 02:12 UTC. <https://grafana.redwood/alerts/1234|tail-latency>. 7% regression on p95 for the svc group for that canary.

ana-ml: after changes: slab_size=192MB, prewarm-swap=true, reserve_pool=256MB, kernel selector: prefer memory-friendly kernel when free < 200MB. rerun numbers: p50 86ms, p95 390ms, p99 720ms, OOMs 0, throughput -1.8%.

mike-runtime: that's a reasonable tradeoff — fewer OOMs, lower eviction churn. can we add an experiment to track KV hit-rate delta vs eviction events? need a per-model metric.

kevin-profiling: added a quick tracer: `kv_evictions_total{model}` + `kv_hit_rate{model}`. initial run shows model mA hit_rate dropped from 0.92 -> 0.61 during eviction spikes.

raj-alloc: long-term we should implement slab compaction during low-load windows and an experimental buffer-reuse pool for kernels that allocate short-lived temps. that reduces peak by reclaiming those ephemeral buffers.

ana-ml: agree. short-term patch: enable buffer_reuse_pool and lower fused_attn tmp alloc threshold. starting a 12h canary on canary1 (gpu0).

deploy-bot: canary rollout started: allocator-tuning/buffer-reuse enabled on canary1 (gpu0). sha: c3d9f2b.

kevin-profiling: quick note — the kernel selector heuristic must be deterministic across hosts or we'll get nondeterministic perf deltas on rollout. add an opt-in flag `--mem-heuristic=enabled` for now.

ana-ml: good call. i'll make it opt-in and wire the flag to the config server for canary.

mike-runtime: next steps: 1) run 24h canary, collect kv_hit_rate per model + eviction counts; 2) if stable, push defrag/slice-compaction to staging; 3) long-term: slab compaction + model pinning in dedicated slots.

sophia-sre: also add an alert for eviction_rate > 5/min to avoid silent regressions.

ana-ml: thanks all. summary: fragmentation + kernel temp buffers triggered OOMs during multi-model co-residency. mitigation = smaller slab slices, reserve pool, buffer_reuse, kernel-memory heuristics, prewarm swap. early canary looks stable. will post full profile after 24h. :party:
